captions: Let's break down the Sunshine Pictures I-P-O —
a two hundred and eighty-two crore mainboard issue from film-maker Vipul Shah's production house.
It's a rare listed play on movies and content —
but with the lumpy earnings that come with the business.
We'll cover what it does, its full financials,
where the money goes, how it's priced,
and whether it fits you.
This is education, not investment advice.
So what does Sunshine do?
It's a Mumbai content house —
it produces and distributes films,
television serials and web series,
led by the film-maker Vipul Shah.
It runs a full production stack in-house: digital colour grading,
Dolby Atmos sound, and dedicated visual-effects pipelines.
And it monetises across every window — theatres,
satellite and TV, streaming platforms, and music,
both in India and overseas.
But keep one thing in mind throughout: a production business is project-dependent,
so its earnings are lumpy — big in a hit year,
thin in a quiet one.
Now the financials — and here you must read carefully.
Total income in FY twenty twenty-six was about seventy-six crore —
and notice,
that's actually DOWN from about a hundred and six crore the year before.
Yet net profit ROSE, to about forty crore.
That mismatch — falling revenue, rising profit —
is classic content economics: it depends on which projects landed in which year.
On the plus side, the balance sheet is clean —
near debt-free,
with a debt-to-equity of just zero point zero six.
Let's put all three statements together.
The income statement carries that lumpiness —
seventy-six crore of income in FY twenty-six,
down from a hundred and six, but forty crore of profit.
The balance sheet is a genuine strength —
net worth of about a hundred and forty-five crore and almost no debt,
just nine crore.
On cash flow,
the fresh issue brings in about a hundred and seventy-three crore,
of which a hundred and twelve and a half crore funds long-term working capital for the content pipeline.
The operating cash-flow line isn't published in the summaries —
read the R-H-P.
Where does your money go?
Of the two hundred and eighty-two crore issue,
about a hundred and seventy-three crore —
roughly sixty-one percent —
is a fresh issue that goes into the company.
The remaining hundred and nine crore is an Offer for Sale,
where the promoter family, Vipul and Shefali Shah,
partly cash out.
So it's a majority-fresh issue —
most of your money funds the content pipeline.
What does the fresh money fund?
The main use — about a hundred and twelve and a half crore —
is long-term working capital: funding the content pipeline,
developing and producing the next slate of films and series.
The rest goes to general corporate purposes.
It makes sense for the business —
more content means more upfront spend before the revenue lands —
but it also means growth depends on making the right content bets.
So how is it priced?
At the top of the band,
Sunshine is valued near one thousand one hundred and twenty-one crore —
about thirty-two and a half times its FY twenty-six earnings.
That is a demanding multiple.
And here's the catch: because earnings are project-dependent,
a P/E built on a single year's profit is fragile —
next year's number rides on which films land.
There also aren't clean listed twins —
pure film-production companies are scarce and messy on the exchanges —
so you can't easily anchor that thirty-two times to a peer group.
Treat the valuation with caution.
So — should you subscribe?
The strengths are real — a near debt-free balance sheet,
an experienced film-maker at the helm,
a full in-house production stack, and it's a rare,
profitable, listed way to play movies and content.
The watch-outs are equally real —
earnings are lumpy and project-dependent,
FY twenty-six revenue actually fell versus the year before,
and at about thirty-two times earnings the price is demanding on a single year's profit.
The takeaway — an interesting,
clean-balance-sheet content play, but a volatile,
hard-to-value one at a full price.
Only you can decide.
Finally — how do you apply, and how much?
Retail investors bid up to two lakh for a thirty-five percent quota,
with allotment by lottery if oversubscribed.
H-N-Is bid above two lakh for a fifteen percent quota.
For Sunshine,
at a three hundred and forty-two to three hundred and sixty rupee band,
one lot works out to about fifteen thousand rupees —
your minimum.
Track the live subscription on the N-S-E and B-S-E I-P-O pages,
Chittorgarh, Moneycontrol, or your broker app.
Let's recap Sunshine Pictures.
Film-maker Vipul Shah's content house — producing movies,
TV and web series with a full in-house production stack and a near debt-free balance sheet.
The issue is about sixty-one percent fresh,
funding the content pipeline.
But remember the two big caveats —
earnings are lumpy and project-dependent,
FY twenty-six revenue fell,
and it's priced at a demanding thirty-two times earnings.
The retail minimum is about fifteen thousand rupees.
This video explains the IPO for education only —
it is not investment advice,
not a buy or sell recommendation,
and not a prediction of listing gains.
Grey-market premium is unofficial and changes hourly.
Always read the RHP and check the live subscription before you apply.
Thanks for watching.
